definitions.sourceCoveredCandidate: All named subject elements for the requirement have a rights-clear reusable evidence route in the current prototype; production quality is not implied.
definitions.partial: Commercially reusable subject evidence exists for a substantial part of the requirement, but one or more named elements still need targeted sourcing or bounded synthesis.
definitions.gap: No current commercial-compatible reusable source route has yet been established for the named requirement.
definitions.sourceSupported: sourceCoveredCandidate + partial; means the requirement is not being built from zero, not that it is complete.

economics.elapsedWorkingTime: not reliably measurable retrospectively across multi-chat governed execution
manualWorkObserved: official course-scope extraction and paraphrase into stable requirement IDs

singleRemainingGap.reason: The model is easy to locate publicly, but the convenient explanatory sources inspected so far use non-commercial licences. A factual lead exists in the original research literature, but a commercial-compatible reusable source route has not yet been established.

interpretation.positiveSignal: 117/118 named requirements already have some commercial-compatible reusable subject evidence. This strongly supports the hypothesis that Psychology does not need to be researched or generated from zero.
interpretation.importantLimit: Only 54/118 are source-complete candidates at the current evidence threshold. The other 63 source-supported requirements still need named-element synthesis or targeted source closure, so 99.2% source support must not be represented as 99.2% finished Foundation coverage.
interpretation.specialistSignal: Options are more fragmented than the compulsory representative topic. The likely production problem is targeted source orchestration and rights verification, not absence of reusable subject truth.
interpretation.nextProof: Resolve a small sample of option partials plus the single remaining gap, then measure transformation into structured Foundation nodes. If closure remains cheap, the useful next investment is automation of source discovery/rights/mapping rather than more general-purpose AI generation.
